fixes.explanation: Close in size, but not what the verse says. The LORD never mentions a king here. He says, "…I will create new heavens and a new earth." Nobody gets a crown in this verse, but the whole sky and ground are what He says He will create.

Yes, a hundred. The LORD says, "For the youth will die at a hundred years…" So in this picture, someone who reaches a hundred is still called a youth. That's a long, full life, and the verse treats it as just the start of the picture.

True, friend. The LORD says, "…he who fails to reach a hundred will be considered accursed." Think about what the verse just said before it: no more infants living only a few days. In this picture, a life that falls short of a hundred is the thing that stands out as unusual. That's how long the LORD says His people's days will be.

That one's actually true. The LORD says, "…he who fails to reach a hundred will be considered accursed." Considered accursed means that dying before a hundred would be seen as a curse. That shows how long the LORD says life will be in this promise.

No giving away here, friend. The LORD says, "They will build houses and dwell in them…" The builders are the ones who dwell in the houses. The next verse adds that they will no longer build houses for others to inhabit. (Isaiah 65:22)

Right, it's false. The LORD says, "Even before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear." So He doesn't wait for them to finish. He answers before they call, and He hears while they are still speaking. I find that comforting.
An eagle doesn't show up in this verse. The LORD says, "The wolf and the lamb will feed together…" The animals feeding together are the wolf and the lamb. The verse names no eagle at all.
True, friend. The LORD says, "…the lion will eat straw like the ox…" A lion eating straw is quite a picture. It's part of the same scene as the wolf and the lamb feeding together.
That one's actually true. The LORD says, "…the lion will eat straw like the ox…" So the lion eats straw the way an ox does. It's right there in the verse.

That one's true. The LORD says, "They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain…" Notice the word all. No spot on that mountain gets left out. After the wolf, the lamb and the lion eating straw, this is where the whole picture lands.
